newsitem.title: USA: US LPGs drift lower to unchanged as rally subsides.
newsitem.headline: US LPGs drift lower to unchanged as rally subsides.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices were lower to unchanged in quiet late trade on Tuesday as the initial panic over news of U.S. military action against Iraq subsided, players said.
Markets were driven up in early trading amid news of the early Tuesday strikes, which were in response to Iraqi attacks over the weekend on a rebel Kurdish controlled town in the north.
The Iraqi aggression led to a suspension of a U.N. oil-for-food scheme that was to allow $2 billion worth of Iraqi oil to flow on the market.

In the Gulf Coast hub of Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane drifted a half cent lower to between 43.00 cents and 43.25 cents a gallon with 43.00 cents sold. Traders noted that 44.00 cent parcels were sold in early dealings.
Conway, Kansas, hub material remained 41.00/41.25 cents, holding onto its one cent morning gain.
"People are buying only limited amounts in case the market comes off more," said one Conway trader.
In Belvieu, most deals were between traders, said one Houston player.
NYMEX October crude oil futures regained some of its intraday momentum before the close, ending up $1.15 at $23.40 a barrel. It had soared $2.00 a barrel in earlier dealings.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859-1631
